patients.summary: Former automotive mechanic with hypertension, chronic alcohol-induced pancreatitis and recurrent depression who joins in 2018 minimizing his drinking. Severe alcohol use disorder is named in 2020, followed by necrotizing pancreatitis, Wernicke encephalopathy, hallucinosis, recurrent pancreatitis and two ethylene glycol poisonings; last seen January 2025.

conditions.label: Major depressive disorder, recurrent, moderate
conditions.note: Per prior records; not on treatment

procedures.procedure: Office visit, new patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
44M new to us, left his old primary office because the hours didn't work with the shop. Works full time as a mechanic.

PMH (his account plus what he brought): high blood pressure for several years, on HCTZ 25 daily, takes it most days. Pancreatitis 'a couple of times' before he came here, told it was from drinking and that the pancreas is now chronically inflamed; no hospital stays in the last year, no current pain. Depression on and off since his 30s, saw a counselor once years ago, nothing current. No surgeries.

Meds: HCTZ 25 mg daily. Allergies: none to medications.
Family: father drank heavily and has cirrhosis; mother has high blood pressure and depression; one sister who has struggled with substances.
Social: married, lives with wife. Quit cigarettes in 2015. Alcohol: says a few beers most nights after work, 'nothing crazy.' AUDIT-C 6. No drugs.
PHQ-9 11: low energy, sleep poor, still working and functioning.

Exam: BP mildly above goal on recheck. Well appearing, no distress. Heart regular, lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. No edema. Mood a little flat, affect appropriate, linear.

A/P
1. HTN: slightly above goal on HCTZ. Continue 25 mg, home cuff if he can get one, recheck in 5-6 months.
2. Chronic pancreatitis by history: quiet now. Explained that the pancreas will keep flaring if he keeps drinking.
3. Alcohol: AUDIT-C positive. He doesn't see his drinking as a problem. Talked through standard drink sizes and the link to his pancreas; gave him the local recovery meeting list. Will revisit.
4. Recurrent depression: moderate symptoms, wants to wait. Revisit next visit.
5. Health maintenance: BMP, CBC, lipids, HCV and HIV screening today. Flu shot given. Records release signed for his prior office.

RTC 5 months.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Mark, your labs from Wednesday look fine: kidney function, salts, blood counts and cholesterol are all in the normal range, and the hepatitis C and HIV screens were negative. See you in the late winter for a blood pressure check.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care office
documents.author: front desk
documents.body:
Received by fax, 14 pages, from the patient's previous primary care office.

Problem list on their summary: hypertension; chronic pancreatitis, alcohol related; major depressive disorder, recurrent, moderate.
Medication list: hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Immunizations on file: influenza in prior seasons; tetanus booster more than ten years ago.
Last visits: blood pressure checks, unremarkable.

Scanned to chart. Routed to PCP.

PCP addendum: Reviewed. Matches what he told me. Tetanus due, will do at his physical.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
BP check. No home cuff yet, wife is looking for one. Taking HCTZ daily, misses maybe once a week. No belly pain since he joined. Busy at the shop through the winter, lots of brake jobs.

Still a few beers most nights by his count; AUDIT-C 7 today, up a point (more on weekends). Not interested in cutting back right now.

BP a little above goal on repeat. Heart RRR, lungs clear, no edema.

A/P: HTN a bit above goal, he admits missed doses; continue HCTZ 25 daily, take it every morning. Alcohol: discussed again, he listened. Physical in the fall with labs.

documents.title: Refill request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: E-refill request from pharmacy, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg #90 with 3 refills. Seen last week. Sent per protocol.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Physical. Missed the June BP visit, says he got called into work.

Feels about the same. Sleep so-so. Mood: PHQ-9 9, a bit better than last year. No abdominal pain, eating fine. Drinking unchanged by his report; AUDIT-C 7.
Meds: HCTZ 25 daily. NKDA.
Social: married, working, quit smoking 2015.

ROS otherwise negative.
Exam: BP acceptable. Weight a little down. Alert, pleasant. HEENT normal. Neck supple. Heart RRR without murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no masses. Skin without rash. Extremities without edema. Neuro nonfocal.

A/P
- HTN: acceptable on HCTZ, continue.
- Alcohol: brief counseling again; still not ready to change.
- Depression: mild-moderate, monitoring.
- Chronic pancreatitis: no flares.
- Prevention: Tdap and flu today. Colon screening: FIT kit given, he prefers that to a scope. CMP and CBC drawn.
RTC 6 months.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Mark, your blood work from the physical came back in the normal range, including liver and kidney tests and blood counts. Please don't forget to send back the stool card.

documents.title: FIT result
documents.author: RN
documents.body: FIT negative. Letter mailed; repeat in one year.

documents.title: Refill
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy asking for HCTZ 25 mg refill, last fill 90 days ago. Approved x90 days. Pt due for 6 month f/u, front desk to call.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
In person (masked, screened at door). First visit since the physical.

CC: can't fall asleep, on edge, hands shaky in the mornings.
HPI: Going on roughly half a year and getting worse. Lies awake, then up at 5 feeling like he never slept. Feels keyed up most days. The shakes are worst first thing and settle by midmorning; he admits a beer helps them. Shop has been slow with the shutdown.
Alcohol: still describes it as a few beers most nights to unwind. When I asked about mornings he went quiet. AUDIT-C 9. No other drugs.
Mood: PHQ-9 13, GAD-7 10.
Meds: HCTZ 25 daily. NKDA.

Exam: BP 140/90, HR 88, BMI 29. Restless, mildly agitated, picking at his hands. Fine tremor of outstretched hands. No jaundice. Several spider angiomas over the upper chest. Liver edge palpable about 2 cm below the right costal margin, smooth, nontender. Spleen not felt. No ascites. Heart regular, lungs clear.

A/P
1. Severe alcohol use disorder with physical dependence. Morning tremor relieved by drinking, sleep and anxiety symptoms, skin and liver findings. Told him plainly that this is what is driving the sleep and nerves. He was not happy to hear it but did not argue. Gave the outpatient program list again and the sober support line. Warned him not to stop suddenly on his own.
2. Enlarged liver, spider angiomas: CBC, liver panel and GGT today.
3. HTN: 140/90, continue HCTZ for now.
4. Depression and anxiety: moderate. He wants to see if sleep improves first.
RTC 3 months, sooner if worse.

documents.title: Liver tests
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: AST 72 > ALT 50, GGT 110, MCV 98, Hgb 13.5. Pattern fits alcohol-related liver injury with the hepatomegaly and angiomas. Adding alcoholic liver disease to the list.

documents.title: Your blood work
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Mark, your liver tests are elevated in the pattern we see when alcohol is irritating the liver, and your red cells are slightly large, which also goes with drinking. Your blood count is otherwise fine. The liver can recover a lot if the drinking comes down. I'd like to recheck in a few months. Call me any time if you want help getting started with cutting back.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Video Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video, he is in his truck on lunch break. Consents to video.

Sleep a bit better on weekends. Tremor 'comes and goes.' Says he cut down to 'three or four' a night, then admitted more on Fridays. AUDIT-C still 9. Did not call the program. PHQ-9 12.
No abdominal pain, eating okay. BP at the pharmacy machine 'in the 130s.'

Observed: alert, talkative, no distress.

A/P: Severe AUD, still precontemplative to contemplative. Kept it brief, left the door open. Depression moderate, stable. Labs deferred, will draw at next in-person. Flu shot this fall at a nurse visit.

documents.title: Nurse Visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu vaccine L deltoid, tolerated. VIS given. Waited 15 min. Reminded him he is due to see the PCP with labs; he will call after the holidays.

events.service: Regional hospital — Emergency Department and Medicine

medications.sig: Take 1 to 2 tablets by mouth every 6 hours as needed for pain, no more than 3,000 mg per day

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital, inpatient medicine. Admitted 4/29/2021 via the ED, discharged 5/3/2021.

Diagnosis: severe acute pancreatitis, alcohol-induced, on a background of chronic pancreatitis. SIRS on presentation.

Presentation: 46-year-old man, two days of intense upper abdominal pain with nausea and repeated vomiting. In the ED he was loud with staff and repeatedly asked for strong opioids, escalating when they were not given right away. Temp 38.3 C, BP 150/90, HR 110, RR 22. Abdomen distended and diffusely tender without rebound or guarding; bowel sounds hypoactive.
Labs: WBC 16.0, Hgb 13.2, plt 230. Amylase 250, lipase 600. AST 120, ALT 100, alk phos 90, T bili 1.2.

Course: aggressive IV fluids, scheduled and as-needed IV analgesia, bowel rest advanced to a low-fat diet by day 3. Monitored on an alcohol withdrawal protocol. Fever and tachycardia settled by day 2.

Discharge medications: hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily (home); acetaminophen 500 mg 1-2 tabs every 6 h as needed, max 3 g/day.
Allergies: NKDA.
Instructions: no alcohol. Follow up with PCP in 1-2 weeks.

Received by fax 5/12/2021; scanned. PCP reviewed: he is already readmitted, see 5/10 phone note.

events.service: Regional hospital — Emergency Department, ICU and Medicine
events.reason: Worsening epigastric pain after recent pancreatitis

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text:
Indication: worsening pancreatitis, fever, hypotension.
Technique: helical CT of the abdomen and pelvis after IV contrast, portal venous phase.
Findings: A large portion of the pancreas fails to enhance, consistent with necrosis, with an associated peripancreatic collection containing locules of gas. No free intraperitoneal air. Liver, spleen, adrenals and kidneys without acute abnormality. Gallbladder unremarkable. No bowel obstruction. Bones unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Large area of pancreatic necrosis with gas within the collection, concerning for infected necrosis.

procedures.procedure: Percutaneous drainage of pancreas using imaging guidance

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital. Admitted 5/7/2021 through the ED; ICU 5/7 to 5/13, then medicine floor. Discharged home 6/4/2021.

Diagnoses: infected pancreatic necrosis complicating severe alcohol-induced acute pancreatitis; moderate protein-calorie malnutrition; chronic pancreatitis; hypertension; alcohol use disorder.

History: 46-year-old man discharged from this hospital 5/3 after alcohol-induced pancreatitis, back with ten days of severe epigastric pain boring through to his back, steadily worse despite the analgesic he went home with, plus nausea and several episodes of vomiting, not bloody or bilious.
On arrival: febrile 38.7 C, HR 112, BP 90/60. Abdomen distended and tender throughout with decreased bowel sounds.
Labs: WBC 18.0, Hgb 13.2, plt 250; amylase 450, lipase 900; CRP 150.
CT with contrast the same evening: large area of pancreatic necrosis with gas in the collection.

Course: fluid resuscitation and IV meropenem in the ICU. CT-guided percutaneous drain placed in the collection 5/11. Nasojejunal tube 5/12 for enteral feeding; nutrition service diagnosed moderate protein-calorie malnutrition. Transferred to the floor 5/13, fevers resolved, meropenem completed. Oral diet resumed in the final week and the feeding tube removed. Withdrawal protocol without complications.

At discharge: drain in place, output low. Follow-up with interventional radiology in about 5 weeks with repeat CT. PCP within 1 week.
Medications: hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily. Allergies: NKDA.
Counseled on complete alcohol abstinence.

CT report attached. Received 6/18/2021 after our records request of 6/9. Scanned, routed to PCP.

documents.title: Call from wife
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Wife called. Mark was in the hospital last week for pancreatitis, went home, and was readmitted Friday with worse pain. Now in the ICU with an infection in the pancreas and they are talking about putting in a drain. She wanted us to know. Asked her to have him call when he is out so we can see him within a week. No discharge paperwork from the first stay yet. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: PCP note
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Noted. Please request records from both admissions.

documents.title: Hospital Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here with wife, five days after a four-week stay. Discharge summary not here yet; history from them and his paperwork.

Two admissions: pancreatitis 4/29 to 5/3, then back 5/7 with infected necrosis, ICU, IV antibiotics, a drain through the left flank, tube feeds for a while. Home 6/4 with the drain still in. Draining a little cloudy fluid, less each day, no fever. Pain much better, mild ache after meals. Eating small low-fat meals, appetite poor. Has lost a lot of weight.
Alcohol: says none since 4/29. Wife nods.
COVID vaccines: two Pfizer doses at the pharmacy in March and April, card shown.

Exam: BP lower than before, afebrile. Weight 79 kg, well down from last year. Thin, tired. Drain site clean, dressing dry, no erythema. Abdomen soft, mildly tender epigastrium, no guarding. No edema. Heart and lungs normal.

A/P
1. Infected pancreatic necrosis with drain: improving. IR follow-up and CT already scheduled per wife. Fever or more pain, call or go in.
2. Moderate protein-calorie malnutrition: per hospital. Small frequent meals, protein with each, an oral supplement twice a day. CMP, CBC today.
3. SIRS from April: resolved.
4. Severe AUD: sober two weeks counting the hospital. Strong encouragement to keep it that way; offered the outpatient program again. He said he would think about it.
5. HTN: lower with the weight loss, keep HCTZ for now.
Records request sent to the hospital for both stays. RTC 2 months.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Mark, your protein level (albumin) is low at 3.0, which fits how much weight you lost in the hospital. Kidney function and salts are fine and your white count is normal now. Liver tests are still a little up. Keep up the small meals and the shakes.

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text:
Comparison: 5/7/2021.
Findings: Percutaneous drain in the peripancreatic collection, which is nearly resolved with only a small residual rim of fluid and no gas. Pancreatic necrosis evolving as expected. No new collection. Liver, spleen and kidneys unremarkable. No bowel obstruction.
reports.conclusion: Peripancreatic collection nearly resolved with drain in place.

documents.title: Interventional radiology letter
documents.author: interventional radiology
documents.body:
Regional hospital interventional radiology clinic, visit 7/13/2021.

Seen for follow-up of a percutaneous drain placed 5/11/2021 for infected pancreatic necrosis. Output has been minimal for about ten days. Afebrile, site clean.
Repeat CT today shows the collection nearly resolved with a small residual rim and no gas.
The drain was removed at the bedside without difficulty; dressing applied.
Plan: no further IR follow-up needed unless symptoms recur. Allergies: NKDA.

Thank you for allowing us to participate in his care.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Drain came out in July, IR letter reviewed: collection nearly gone. No fevers. Belly fine most days, occasional ache after a heavy meal.

Back at the shop part time. Drinking again: 'just beer, just on weekends' at first, now most nights again by his wife's account at the last call. AUDIT-C 9. PHQ-9 12.
Weight up a little.

Exam: BP at goal. Thin. Healed drain scar left flank. Abdomen soft, nontender. Heart and lungs normal.

A/P
1. Acute necrotizing pancreatitis episode: resolved, closing both acute problems. Chronic pancreatitis remains.
2. Malnutrition: slowly improving, keep supplements.
3. Severe AUD: drinking again after the hospital. Long talk about the pancreas, what another attack could mean. He wants to do it on his own. Program list again.
4. HTN: fine on HCTZ.
5. Depression: unchanged, he declines to discuss more today.
CMP, GGT today. RTC 3-4 months. Flu shot in the fall.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Albumin is up to 3.4, good progress. Liver tests about where they were. Kidneys fine.

documents.title: Refill and scheduling
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pt called for HCTZ refill, out in 3 days. Sent 90 days per protocol. Offered flu shot appointment, he said not this year. Overdue for follow-up, booked for February.

events.service: Regional hospital — Emergency Department and Medicine

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth daily for 3 months

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital. Admitted 4/25/2022 from the ED; discharged 5/2/2022.

Principal diagnosis: Wernicke encephalopathy.
Other: alcohol use disorder, chronic pancreatitis with infected necrosis in 2021, protein-calorie malnutrition, hypertension, depression.

HPI: 47-year-old man brought in for two days of muddled thinking, staggering and seeing double. He had been eating hardly anything for several weeks because of nausea and vomiting.
ED: vital signs within normal limits. Oriented to self only, not to time or place. Nystagmus on lateral gaze, broad-based unsteady gait. No signs of head trauma.
Labs: glucose 250, Na 140, K 4.0, creatinine 1.0, AST 80, ALT 35. A thiamine level was not sent.
IV fluids with dextrose were started in the ED, and over the next few hours he became more confused. Wernicke encephalopathy was recognized and high-dose IV thiamine was begun.

Course: IV thiamine three times daily, then daily. Confusion cleared over several days; diplopia resolved. Gait improved, still a little wide-based at discharge; walking independently. Withdrawal protocol, uneventful. Diet tolerated.

Discharge meds: thiamine 100 mg by mouth daily for 3 months; hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA. PCP follow-up 1 week. Advised strongly to stop drinking.

Scanned 5/6/2022, routed to PCP.

documents.title: Hospital Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Wife drove him. Discharge summary reviewed: Wernicke encephalopathy, IV thiamine, home on oral thiamine 100 daily for three months.

He remembers little of the first days in hospital. Thinking 'back to normal' per him, wife says he repeats himself a little less each day. Double vision gone. Still a bit wobbly on stairs, using the railing. Eating better, nausea mostly gone. Taking thiamine and HCTZ.
Alcohol: had a couple of beers since coming home. AUDIT-C 10 for the past year. PHQ-9 14.

Exam: BP fine. Weight 74 kg, down again. Alert, oriented x3, conversant, recalls 3/3 at five minutes. No nystagmus today. Gait slightly broad, steady with turns, can tandem a few steps. Heart and lungs normal. Abdomen soft.

A/P
1. Wernicke encephalopathy: much improved, mild residual gait unsteadiness. Continue thiamine 100 daily to finish the course. No driving until his gait is clearly normal; he agreed.
2. Severe AUD: drinking again within days. I was direct that the next episode could leave permanent memory damage. He teared up, but declined referral today.
3. Malnutrition: weight 74 kg, albumin check today.
4. Depression: PHQ-9 14. He says he is 'disgusted with himself.' Denies thoughts of hurting himself.
5. HTN: at goal, continue.
CMP, CBC, GGT. RTC 3 months.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Mark, your kidney tests and salts are normal. Albumin is 3.2, a bit lower than last summer, so keep eating protein at every meal. Liver tests are still elevated, about the same pattern as before.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Three months out from the Wernicke admission. Finished the thiamine bottle this week. Gait normal to him, no falls, back to driving short distances. Memory fine per him. Working most days.
Still drinking, won't quantify. PHQ-9 13.

Exam: BP at goal, weight up slightly. Oriented, conversant. Gait normal, tandem okay, stands steady with eyes closed. Abdomen soft.

A/P
1. Wernicke: recovered clinically. Thiamine course done, stopping it.
2. AUD: ongoing, same conversation, same answer.
3. HTN: at goal.
4. Depression: moderate, stable.
5. FIT kit given, last one 2019.
RTC 3 months.

documents.title: FIT result
documents.author: RN
documents.body: FIT negative. Portal message sent.

documents.title: Call from sister
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Patient's sister called. She took him to the ED yesterday: he had gone about a day without drinking, which she said never happens, and started seeing bugs on the walls and hearing voices. ED watched him and sent him home. She is worried and wants him seen. Booked with PCP 11/9. ED records requested.

documents.title: ED discharge instructions (patient copy)
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Patient-provided printout, regional hospital emergency department, visit 11/1/2022.

Your diagnosis today: alcoholic hallucinosis.
Your tests: blood counts normal; electrolytes normal; liver tests mildly elevated; alcohol level not detected.
Instructions: Do not stop drinking suddenly on your own without medical help. Return for confusion, seizures, fever or if hallucinations return. Follow up with your primary care doctor this week.

Scanned at check-in. The full ED record has not been received.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: ED Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
48M here after an ED visit 11/1, brought by his sister then. Has the ED instruction sheet only (scanned): alcoholic hallucinosis, counts and lytes normal, LFTs mildly up, alcohol not detected.

His story: tried to go a day without drinking, by evening saw bugs crawling on the walls and heard people talking in the next room when no one was there. Scared him. Knew where he was the whole time. Started drinking again the next day and the visions stopped. No seizures. No hallucinations since.
AUDIT-C 10. PHQ-9 13, denies thoughts of self-harm.

Exam: BP okay. Calm, oriented x3, slight fine tremor of the hands. No nystagmus. Gait normal. Abdomen soft.

A/P
1. Alcoholic hallucinosis: happened when he stopped abruptly. Explained that stopping safely needs medical supervision and that the next time could be worse. Offered to help him get into a detox and program. He wants to talk it over with his wife.
2. Severe AUD: as above.
3. ALD: CMP and GGT today.
4. HTN, depression: stable.
Flu shot today. ED record requested again. RTC 3 months.

documents.title: Refill
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Electronic request, HCTZ 25 mg #90. Last seen November. Sent per protocol; front desk to book his physical.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Physical, first since 2019. ED record from November never came; we have the instruction sheet only.

Interval: no hospital stays since November. No more hallucinations. Belly quiet except the odd ache after fried food. Working steady at the garage, says it keeps him busy.
Alcohol: 'about the same.' AUDIT-C 10. No withdrawal symptoms he will admit to.
Mood: PHQ-9 10, best in a while. Denies thoughts of self-harm.
Meds: HCTZ 25 daily. NKDA. Former smoker, quit 2015.

ROS: no chest pain, no dyspnea, no melena, no jaundice.
Exam: BP okay. Weight up a little. Alert, oriented. Skin: spider angiomas on the chest as before, no jaundice. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender; liver edge just palpable. No ascites, no edema. Gait normal.

A/P
1. Severe AUD: unchanged. Brief counseling. Offered referral, declined.
2. Alcoholic liver disease: CMP, GGT, CBC today.
3. Chronic pancreatitis, malnutrition history: weight recovering slowly.
4. Wernicke encephalopathy (2022), alcoholic hallucinosis (2022): no recurrence.
5. HTN: fine on HCTZ.
6. Depression: mild-moderate today.
7. Prevention: PCV20 today given alcohol use and liver disease. FIT due again 2024. Lipids today.
RTC 6 months.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Mark, kidney function, salts, blood counts and cholesterol are fine. Liver tests are still elevated in the same alcohol-related pattern, not worse. Your protein level is better than last year.

events.service: Regional hospital — Emergency Department and Medicine

medications.sig: Dissolve 1 tablet on the tongue every 8 hours as needed for nausea

reports.text:
Indication: pancreatitis.
Findings: Gallbladder without stones, wall not thickened, no pericholecystic fluid. Common bile duct normal caliber; no intrahepatic biliary ductal dilatation. Liver normal in size. Pancreas partly obscured by bowel gas. Spleen and kidneys unremarkable. No ascites.
reports.conclusion: No gallstones. No biliary ductal dilatation.

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital. Admission 10/24/2023 to 10/29/2023.

Diagnosis: acute alcohol-induced pancreatitis, recurrent, on chronic pancreatitis.
History includes infected necrosis in 2021 managed with a percutaneous drain, Wernicke encephalopathy 2022, alcohol use disorder, hypertension, depression, malnutrition.

Presented after a day of steady, severe upper abdominal pain going through to the back with nausea and vomiting. Eating made it worse; sitting forward eased it a little.
ED: BP 90/60, HR 115, temp 38.2 C. Appeared uncomfortable and distressed. Epigastric tenderness, bowel sounds diminished.
Labs: WBC 16.0, Hgb 13.5, plt 250. Amylase 900, lipase 850. AST 120, ALT 90. BUN 25, creatinine 1.2.
RUQ/abdominal ultrasound: no gallstones and no biliary duct dilation.

Course: IV fluids with prompt hemodynamic response, IV analgesia, antiemetics, withdrawal protocol. Diet advanced day 3. No imaging evidence of a new collection was sought; clinically improving.
Discharge 10/29: home. Medications: hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily; ondansetron 4 mg ODT every 8 h as needed for nausea.
Allergies: NKDA. Follow up with PCP. Abstinence advised.

Received 12/6/2023 after second request. Scanned, routed to PCP.

documents.title: Refill request, ondansetron
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy faxed a refill request for ondansetron 4 mg ODT, original prescriber is a hospitalist at the regional hospital, filled 10/29. Not on our med list. Called pt: he was admitted 10/24 to 10/29 with pancreatitis again. Booked hospital follow-up 11/14. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: PCP note
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Did not know about this admission. Will address refill at the visit. Please request the discharge summary.

documents.title: Hospital Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Learned of the October admission from a pharmacy refill request. Summary not here; per him: pancreatitis again, five days, fluids and pain medicine, ultrasound showed no gallstones. Home 10/29 with nausea pills, used most of them the first week, now rarely needed.

Pain gone. Eating, though less than before. Lost weight again.
Alcohol: resumed after discharge, 'less.' AUDIT-C 10. PHQ-9 13, no thoughts of self-harm.

Exam: afebrile, BP up a little today. Thinner. Abdomen soft, mild epigastric tenderness, no guarding. Skin no jaundice.

A/P
1. Recurrent acute alcohol pancreatitis: resolved clinically. Third hospital stay for the pancreas. Told him straight that each attack takes more of the gland.
2. Ondansetron: he has enough left, no refill needed.
3. Severe AUD: same. Program list, his choice.
4. Malnutrition: weight down again, encourage supplements.
5. Depression: moderate.
CMP, CBC today. Flu shot today. Hospital records requested again. RTC 3-4 months.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Mark, white count and kidney function are back to normal after the hospital. Liver tests are elevated as before.

documents.title: Refill and appointment
documents.author: patient
documents.body: need my blood pressure pill refilled, pharmacy said they need ok from you. sorry I missed scheduling, can I come in may sometime

documents.title: Re: Refill and appointment
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Hi Mark, the refill was sent this morning. You're booked May 22 at 1:40 with your doctor.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Six months since the last visit. No hospital visits. October discharge summary finally came in December, matches his account.

Feeling okay. Belly fine. Drinking 'normal for me.' AUDIT-C 10. PHQ-9 12, denies thoughts of self-harm.
Meds: HCTZ 25. NKDA.

Exam: BP a little higher than last year. Weight back up some. Alert, oriented. Spider angiomas unchanged. Liver edge just palpable. No edema.

A/P
1. HTN: borderline today, continue HCTZ 25, recheck next visit.
2. Severe AUD, ALD: counseling; CMP and GGT today.
3. Depression: moderate, stable.
4. Chronic pancreatitis: quiet.
5. Turned 50 next month: Shingrix #1 today, #2 in 2-6 months. FIT due; declined a kit today, will do it next time.
RTC 6 months.

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary
documents.author: critical care
documents.body:
Regional hospital. ED arrival 11/1/2024, ICU 11/1 to 11/5, medicine floor, discharged home 11/8/2024.

Diagnoses: ethylene glycol poisoning, intent undetermined; acute kidney injury; high anion gap metabolic acidosis. Background: severe alcohol use disorder, chronic pancreatitis, prior Wernicke encephalopathy and alcoholic hallucinosis, depression, hypertension.

Presentation: brought in by his wife for sudden confusion and labored breathing. She described him as low since losing his job over the summer and drinking more than usual; she did not know what he had been drinking.
T 37.2 C, BP 140/90, HR 110, RR 28. Breathing fast, faintly sweet smell to the breath, disoriented to time and place, tender over both flanks.
Urinalysis: calcium oxalate crystals. Calcium 7.0, creatinine 2.5, arterial pH 7.25, anion gap 24.

Course: fomepizole started in the ED. Nephrology placed a temporary dialysis catheter and he received hemodialysis in the ICU with clearing of the acidosis. Mental status returned to baseline by day 3. Creatinine improved to 1.6 by discharge. Psychiatry saw him on the floor; the question of intent was not settled in their note, and he was discharged home with his wife and outpatient follow-up.

Discharge medications: hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily. Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: PCP within 1-2 weeks with a BMP; outpatient mental health and substance use treatment strongly recommended.

Received 11/20/2024. Scanned, routed to PCP.

documents.title: Call from wife
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Spoke with his wife. He was in the ICU 11/1 to 11/8, poisoned by antifreeze per the doctors, needed dialysis, home now. She doesn't know whether he meant to. He lost his job at the garage over the summer and has been down and drinking more. He is home with her, sleeping a lot, eating some. She has cleared the garage of the automotive fluids. I asked her to call 911 for any confusion or if he talks about hurting himself, and gave her the crisis line. Booked 11/19 with a BMP. Records requested.

orders.reason: Worsening recurrent depression after ethylene glycol ingestion

documents.title: Hospital Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
With wife. Discharge summary not yet received; history from both and his paperwork. ICU 11/1-11/8 for ethylene glycol (antifreeze) poisoning, fomepizole and dialysis, kidney function recovering at discharge. Saw psychiatry in the hospital.

He says he does not remember what he drank that night and gets quiet when asked if he meant to. Lost his job at the garage in the summer; money tight. Sleeping a lot, little interest in anything. PHQ-9 17. Asked directly: no current thoughts of killing himself, no plan; says he wants to be around for his wife. Wife has removed the fluids from the garage and there are no guns in the house.
Alcohol: some beer since discharge. AUDIT-C 11.
No flank pain now, urinating normally.

Exam: Weight 71 kg. Tired, flat affect, makes eye contact, linear. Oriented x3. No nystagmus. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. No flank tenderness. Healing catheter site right neck. No edema.

A/P
1. Ethylene glycol poisoning, intent unclear, s/p fomepizole and dialysis. Safety plan reviewed with both; crisis line numbers given again.
2. AKI: BMP today.
3. Recurrent major depression, worse: PHQ-9 17. Placing psychiatry referral today; he agreed to be called.
4. Severe AUD: addiction medicine referral placed as well. Wife supportive.
5. HTN: BP up today, in pain and under stress; continue HCTZ, recheck next visit.
6. Flu shot today.
RTC 6-8 weeks, sooner as needed.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Mark, your creatinine is 1.4, better than the 1.6 when you left the hospital. Salts and blood counts are fine. We'll recheck at your next visit. The psychiatry and addiction medicine offices should call you this week.

documents.title: Referral phone numbers
documents.author: patient
documents.body: This is his wife writing on his account. Nobody called him about the psychiatry or the addiction appointments. Can you send the numbers so we can call ourselves?

documents.title: Re: Referral phone numbers
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Hi, both referrals were sent on 11/19. Here are the intake lines: psychiatry 413-555-0161, addiction medicine 413-555-0174. Mention his name and date of birth and that his primary care doctor sent the referral.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seven weeks after the ICU stay. Discharge summary reviewed since last visit: fomepizole, dialysis, psychiatry consult without a firm conclusion on intent, creatinine 1.6 at discharge.

He came alone. Has not called either referral; wife called psychiatry once and was put on a waitlist, he says. Looking for work, nothing yet. Mood low, PHQ-9 15. No thoughts of self-harm, no plan, safety plan still on the fridge. Drinking about the same as before the hospital. AUDIT-C 11.
No urinary symptoms. Appetite fair.

Exam: BP borderline. Weight steady. Flat but engaged, oriented. Heart and lungs normal. No edema.

A/P
1. AKI: creatinine today; if normal, resolved.
2. Ethylene glycol poisoning 11/2024: no repeat, garage cleared.
3. Recurrent major depression: still moderately severe. Encouraged him to call psychiatry himself; numbers given again.
4. Severe AUD: addiction medicine referral still open, encouraged.
5. HTN: continue HCTZ.
6. Shingrix #2 overdue; he wants to wait.
RTC 2-3 months.

documents.title: Creatinine
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Creatinine 1.1, back to his usual. AKI resolved.

documents.title: Your labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Mark, your kidney test is back to normal at 1.1. Please call the psychiatry and addiction medicine numbers when you can, and book a visit for March.

documents.title: Refill
documents.author: MA
documents.body: E-refill request HCTZ 25 mg #90. Last visit 1/8, March follow-up never booked. Sent per protocol, left voicemail to schedule.

documents.title: Time for a follow-up
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Hi Mark, our records show you're overdue for a follow-up visit with your doctor. Please call or reply here and we'll find a time that works.

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary
documents.author: critical care
documents.body:
Regional hospital. ED 10/27/2025, ICU 10/27 to 10/31, then medicine; discharged 11/4/2025.

Diagnosis: ethylene glycol poisoning, second episode (first 11/2024). High anion gap metabolic acidosis with an osmolar gap.
Background per our records: severe alcohol use disorder, chronic pancreatitis, Wernicke encephalopathy, alcoholic hallucinosis, recurrent depression, hypertension, malnutrition.

Presentation: wife found him confused and struggling to breathe in the garage, several empty containers of car products nearby. She reports he has been depressed and out of work since losing his job last year, with ongoing heavy drinking.
BP 130/85, HR 110, RR 30, T 37.2 C, SpO2 94% on room air. Rapid breathing, faint sweet breath odor, myoclonic jerks, horizontal nystagmus.
Labs: Na 140, K 4.2, Cl 98, HCO3 12, creatinine 1.8. Serum osmolality 320 measured vs 290 calculated. Anion gap 30. Urine microscopy: calcium oxalate crystals.

Course: fomepizole, hemodialysis via a temporary catheter, ICU monitoring; mentation cleared. Psychiatry consulted. Discharged home with his wife.
Discharge medications: hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily. Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: PCP; outpatient psychiatry and substance use treatment.

Received by fax 12/3/2025. Scanned to chart, routed to PCP.

PCP: Reviewed. Second ingestion. He has not been seen here since January. Will reach out.

documents.title: Checking in
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Mark, I received the records from your hospital stay in October and November. I'd like to see you, and I can fit you in this week. Please call the office or reply here. If you're having thoughts of hurting yourself, call 988 or go to the emergency room.

documents.title: Refill
documents.author: MA
documents.body: E-refill request HCTZ 25 mg. Last visit 1/8/2025, no reply to the December message. Per PCP, 30-day supply only, needs a visit and labs before more. Voicemail left.

documents.title: Refill
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy requesting HCTZ again. Discussed with PCP: 30 days sent so he isn't without it. Called home number, spoke with wife, who will have him call to book. No appointment made yet.
